entries.title: Psalms 37:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Fret not - Because they prosper in their wicked enterprizes.

entries.title: Psalms 37:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Commit - All thy cares and business, and necessities, commend to God by fervent prayer.

entries.title: Psalms 37:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Judgment - It shall be as visible to men, as the light of the sun, at noon - day.

entries.title: Psalms 37:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rest - Do not repine at his dealings, but quietly submit to his will, and wait for his help.

entries.title: Psalms 37:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Fret not - Either against the sinner for his success; or against God. Do evil - If grief arise in thee, take care that it do not transport thee to sin.

entries.title: Psalms 37:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The earth - This for the most part was literally fulfilled in that state of the church.

entries.title: Psalms 37:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Not be - He shall be dead and gone. Diligently - Industriously seeking him. His place - His place and estate, and glory.

entries.title: Psalms 37:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: But - Those who patiently bear God's afflicting hand, and meekly pass by injuries. Peace - Partly of outward peace and prosperity, which God in his due time will give them: but principally of inward peace, in the sense of God's favour and the assurance of endless happiness.

entries.title: Psalms 37:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: His day - The day appointed by God for his punishment or destruction.

entries.title: Psalms 37:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Knoweth - Observes with care and affection. The days - All things which befal them, their dangers and fears, and suffering. For ever - To them and their seed for ever: and when they die their inheritance is not lost, but exchanged for one infinitely better.

entries.title: Psalms 37:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Fat - Which in an instant melts before the fire.

entries.title: Psalms 37:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Established - So that he shall not fall into mischief.

entries.title: Psalms 37:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Fall - Into trouble.

entries.title: Psalms 37:25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Forsaken - These temporal promises, were more express to the Jews in the times of the Old Testament, than to Christians.

entries.title: Psalms 37:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Blessed - Not only with spiritual, but with temporal blessings.

entries.title: Psalms 37:27
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Dwell - Thou shalt dwell in the land, and afterwards in heaven.

entries.title: Psalms 37:30
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The mouth - Having shewed, God's singular care over the righteous, he proceeds to give a character of them. Judgment - Of God's judgment, word or law.

entries.title: Psalms 37:31
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Heart - His thoughts, meditations and affections are fixed upon it. Slide - Slide, or swerve, from the rule, from God's law.

entries.title: Psalms 37:35
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bay - tree - Which is continually green and flourishing even in winter.

entries.title: Psalms 37:36
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Yet - He was gone in an instant. But - There was no monument or remainder of him left.

entries.title: Psalms 37:37
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Peace - Though he may meet with troubles in his way, yet all shall end well.

entries.title: Psalms 37:38
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Together - All without exception.
